findings.text: Each routed header establishes a single inclusion guard macro that is defined on first inclusion to suppress repeat processing. The tnum, topology, TPM core, TPM buffer, and TPM command headers each follow this pattern with distinct guard names.
The tnum record holds two 64-bit members named value and mask. Value carries known data bits while mask marks unknown positions, so certainty is derived by combining both members.
Predicates tnum_is_unknown and tnum_subreg_is_const are available to includers for querying tristate numbers. One tests whole-value unknown status and the other tests low subregister constness.

Unknown status holds exactly when every mask bit is set, indicating no known bit. Subregister constness holds exactly when the derived subregister view carries a zero mask. The subregister derivation helper itself is not shown in these fragments.
LOCAL_DISTANCE is ten, REMOTE_DISTANCE is twenty, DISTANCE_BITS is eight, RECLAIM_DISTANCE is thirty, and PENALTY_FOR_NODE_WITH_CPUS is one.

Distance lookup through node_distance returns the local constant when source and target nodes match and the remote constant otherwise. The per-node CPU count through nr_cpus_node is the weight of the node CPU mask.

Includers gain inline NUMA accessors. Writers set_numa_node, set_cpu_numa_node, set_numa_mem, and set_cpu_numa_mem publish node and memory affinity, while readers cpu_to_mem and topology_get_cpu_scale query memory node and capacity scale.

Node writers update per-CPU state, with current-CPU forms affecting the executing processor and indexed forms affecting the named processor. One cpu_to_mem variant consults per-CPU memory state while the alternate delegates to the CPU to node mapping, so the two agree only when memory and CPU mappings coincide. Capacity scale reads per-CPU scale state.

TOPOLOGY_DIE_SYSFS, TOPOLOGY_CLUSTER_SYSFS, TOPOLOGY_BOOK_SYSFS, and TOPOLOGY_DRAWER_SYSFS are unconditionally present. Fallback identifiers report minus one for topology_physical_package_id, topology_die_id, topology_cluster_id, topology_book_id, and topology_drawer_id, zero for topology_core_id, and zero for topology_ppin.

Default hierarchy masks are singletons containing only the queried CPU for sibling, core, cluster, die, book, and drawer levels. One cpu_smt_mask variant follows the sibling mask while the alternate returns the singleton directly. Node mask lookup resolves through CPU to node translation to the node mask.

Primary thread election through topology_is_primary_thread selects the lowest numbered sibling as primary, so exactly one member of each SMT group qualifies. Architectures with a distinguished primary thread are expected to override this default, and offline CPU sibling contents depend on whether generic topology construction is used.

The nth CPU helper sched_numa_find_nth_cpu ignores its node argument and selects the nth set bit from the intersection of the supplied set with the online set. The hop mask helper sched_numa_hop_mask in this configuration never succeeds and reports operation not supported.

Node by distance iteration through for_each_node_numadist starts from a given node, repeatedly selects the nearest unvisited node, clears it from the unvisited set, and stops after the maximum node count. Hop mask iteration through for_each_numa_hop_mask starts at zero hops, yields the online set for the no-node start case and otherwise queries the hop helper, advancing the hop count until absence or failure is reported.

The driver operations table tpm_class_ops opens with flags plus completion bytes req_complete_mask and req_complete_val. It then provides operations req_canceled, recv, send, cancel, status, update_timeouts, update_durations, go_idle, cmd_ready, request_locality, relinquish_locality, and clk_enable for cancellation testing, byte transfer, abort, status sampling, timeout refresh, duration refresh, idle entry, ready entry, locality claim, locality release, and clock gating. Flags support TPM_OPS_AUTO_STARTUP for automatic startup.

Session workspace tpm_space holds context_tbl and session_tbl tables with companion pointers context_buf and session_buf plus size buf_size. BIOS log window tpm_bios_log pairs bios_event_log with bios_event_log_end. Sequence wrapper tpm_chip_seqops pairs chip with seqops. Hash descriptor tpm2_hash pairs crypto_id with tpm_id.

Logging follows with log plus bin_log_seqops and ascii_log_seqops. Identity follows with flags, dev_num, and is_open single-open marker. Firmware upgrade status through tpm_is_firmware_upgrade reflects the dedicated flag bit. Handle classification through tpm2_handle_mso extracts the top byte as the octet type. Return normalization through tpm2_rc_value clears bit seven when set. Error translation through tpm_ret_to_err passes negative values through, maps success to zero, session memory shortage to out of memory, hash failure to invalid argument, and all other codes to permission denied. Container recovery through to_tpm_chip derives the chip record from its embedded device member. Auth accessor through tpm2_chip_auth yields the chip session pointer when HMAC support is present and null otherwise.

Fallback builds without TPM services expose query entry points that uniformly report absence. Probes tpm_is_tpm2, tpm_pcr_read, tpm_pcr_extend, and tpm_get_random report missing device, default lookup tpm_default_chip yields null, and empty auth appender tpm_buf_append_empty_auth performs no action.

The active empty auth appender extends the command buffer with a nine byte authorization trailer naming the supplied handle and carrying empty nonce, attributes, and authentication fields. The fallback variant leaves the buffer unchanged.

In the no-HMAC configuration the authorization session machine is degenerate. Start through tpm2_start_auth_session reports success, end through tpm2_end_auth_session does nothing, fill through tpm_buf_fill_hmac_session reports success, and check through tpm_buf_check_hmac_response returns the incoming status unchanged, so callers observe no state transition.

Driver callbacks beneath ops require holding the chip read write semaphore ops_sem, with sysfs paths acquiring it implicitly, and the pointer is cleared on driver unregister so lookup must validate presence. Command serialization uses tpm_mutex, and is_open permits only one concurrent opener.

Clearing ops while sysfs or command paths run risks use after clear unless semaphore discipline is observed. Marking a command buffer with TPM_BUF_INVALID permanently disables further appends. Firmware upgrade and suspend flags alter power and availability assumptions, so callers must revalidate chip state after observing them.

Hop mask callers must treat error pointer returns as absence and test with error or null checks before dereference, as for_each_numa_hop_mask does. Primary thread election assumes sibling masks include the queried CPU itself, which holds only on generic topology builds. The nth CPU helper discards its node argument, so callers cannot rely on node filtering.
